name: selector names: the one name that fails both the charset and the ban list is refused everywhere

acknowledged_divergence.reason: Contract §18.23 item 241: `approve_consequential` is the only name that fails the choice-name charset AND the flag-name ban list, and the order the two run in is structural rather than chosen. A Go member choice is spelled MemberChoice(StringFlag("approve_consequential", ...), ...), and StringFlag runs its own name validation at CONSTRUCTION, so the ban fires before a MemberChoiceFlag -- the only thing that could hold a charset check -- exists at all. Moving Go's bans out of the flag constructors would reach the charset first and would also move every ban off the line that writes the bad name. Both implementations refuse the declaration and no program exists that one accepts and another runs, so the case asserts the refusal everywhere and stops asserting byte-identity across the sentence.
